lessons.title: Portfolio Diversification
lessons.description: Learn how spreading investments across assets reduces risk without sacrificing returns.

content.text: Don't Put All Your Eggs in One Basket

**Diversification** is the practice of spreading your investments across multiple assets so that a catastrophic loss in one doesn't wipe out your entire portfolio. In crypto, this is especially important given how volatile individual coins can be.
🧺 How to Diversify a Crypto Portfolio

**By asset type:**
- Large caps (BTC, ETH) — Core holdings, more stable
- Mid caps — Established altcoins with real use cases
- Small caps — Higher risk/reward
- Stablecoins (USDC, USDT) — Preserve value, buy dips

**By sector:**
- Layer 1 blockchains (Solana, Avalanche)
- DeFi protocols (Uniswap, Aave)
- Infrastructure (Chainlink, The Graph)

A common starting allocation: 50–60% BTC/ETH, 30–40% quality altcoins, 10% stablecoins.
⚖️ Rebalancing

**Rebalancing** means periodically returning your portfolio to your target allocation. If BTC rises from 50% to 70% of your portfolio, you might sell some BTC and buy underperforming assets to maintain your target split.

**Correlation** matters: assets that move together don't provide true diversification. Bitcoin and most altcoins are highly correlated — when BTC falls, most alts fall harder. True diversification might include uncorrelated assets like stablecoins or real-world assets.

lessons.title: Position Sizing & Risk Per Trade
lessons.description: Learn how to size your trades to protect capital and survive losing streaks.

content.text: The Most Important Skill: Sizing Your Trades

Even great strategy fails if you risk too much on a single trade. **Position sizing** is deciding how much of your capital to put into each trade. Get this right and even a losing streak won't destroy your account. Get it wrong and one bad trade ends your trading career.
📏 The 1% Rule

The **1% rule**: never risk more than 1% of your total portfolio on a single trade. On a $1,000 portfolio, that's $10 max risk per trade.

This means that even 10 losing trades in a row only costs you 10% of your portfolio — painful but survivable. Traders who risk 10–20% per trade can be wiped out in just a few losses.

**Risk vs Position Size** — These are different:
- Your position size is how much crypto you buy
- Your risk is how much you lose if your stop-loss hits
- Example: Buy $200 of BTC with a stop 5% below entry → risk = $10 (1% of $1,000)
⚠️ Leverage

**Leverage** lets you control a larger position than your capital. 10x leverage means $100 controls $1,000. But it also means a 10% move against you wipes out your entire position.

**For beginners, avoid leverage entirely.** Even professional traders have been destroyed by it in crypto's volatile markets. If you must use leverage, use no more than 2–3x and maintain strict stop-losses.

**Risk-reward ratio** — Only take trades where potential gain is at least 2× the potential loss. This means you can lose more often than you win and still be profitable.

lessons.title: Stop Losses & Take Profit
lessons.description: Learn to use stop-losses and take-profit orders to protect gains and limit downside.

content.text: Automate Your Discipline

The biggest cause of trading losses isn't bad analysis — it's bad execution. Traders who know what to do, but don't do it when emotions take over, consistently lose money. **Stop-loss and take-profit orders** remove emotion from the equation by automating your exits in advance.
🛑 Stop-Loss Orders

A **stop-loss** automatically sells your position when the price drops to your set level, capping your loss.

**Where to place it:** Below a key support level — somewhere the price reaching there invalidates your trade thesis. Not too close (normal volatility triggers it) and not too far (turns a small loss into a big one).

**Trailing stop-loss:** Moves upward as price rises, locking in profits dynamically. If price drops by a set %, it triggers. Great for letting profits run while protecting gains.

**Breakeven stop:** Once a trade is +10–20% in profit, move your stop-loss to your entry price. Now the trade can't lose money.
🎯 Take-Profit Orders

A **take-profit** automatically sells when the price hits your target, locking in gains without you needing to watch the screen.

**Partial take-profits:** Sell 50% at the first target, let the rest run to a higher target. This books real profit while keeping exposure to further upside.

**Letting profits run** means not closing too early out of anxiety — one of the hardest disciplines in trading, but essential for good returns when you're right.

lessons.title: Crypto Scams & Security
lessons.description: Recognize common crypto scams and learn security best practices to protect your funds.

content.text: In Crypto, Security Is Your Responsibility

Traditional banking has fraud protection — if someone steals from your account, the bank can often reverse it. In crypto, **transactions are irreversible**. If someone steals your crypto, it's gone forever. This makes security knowledge essential for every crypto user.
🎣 Common Crypto Scams

**Phishing** — Fake websites or messages impersonating legitimate services to steal your login credentials or seed phrase. Always check the URL carefully.

**Pump and Dump** — A group artificially inflates a coin's price by buying heavily and spreading hype, then sells at the top, crashing the price for late buyers.

**Rug Pull** — Developers launch a project, attract investor money, then abandon it and disappear with the funds.

**Honeypot** — A token you can buy but the smart contract prevents selling. You're trapped.

**Ponzi Scheme** — Pays early investors with new investor money. Always collapses when new money stops coming in.
🔐 Security Best Practices

- **Never share your seed phrase or private key** — No legitimate service will ever ask for these
- **Use a hardware wallet** for significant amounts
- **Enable 2FA** — Use an authenticator app (not SMS) — SIM swapping can steal SMS codes
- **Verify URLs carefully** before entering any credentials
- **Use unique, strong passwords** for every exchange (use a password manager)
- **If it sounds too good to be true, it is** — Guaranteed returns don't exist in crypto

lessons.title: Regulation & Taxes Overview
lessons.description: Understand the basics of crypto regulation and tax obligations around the world.

content.text: Crypto Has Rules — Even If They're Still Evolving

Cryptocurrency is decentralized, but the people who use it aren't exempt from the law. Governments around the world are developing regulations for crypto — and in most countries, **crypto gains are taxable**. Ignoring this is a serious mistake.
🏛️ Regulation Basics

**KYC (Know Your Customer)** — Exchanges must verify user identities to comply with financial regulations and prevent money laundering.

**AML (Anti-Money Laundering)** — Rules requiring exchanges to monitor and report suspicious activity.

**SEC (US)** — The Securities and Exchange Commission. It argues that many cryptocurrencies are securities and fall under its jurisdiction.

**CBDC (Central Bank Digital Currency)** — Government-issued digital currencies (like a digital dollar). Different from decentralized crypto — they are centralized and controlled by governments.
💰 Crypto Taxes

**Taxable events** typically include:
- Selling crypto for fiat (USD, EUR, etc.)
- Trading one crypto for another
- Spending crypto on goods or services
- Receiving crypto as income or mining rewards

**Capital gains tax:**
- Short-term (held <1 year): taxed at your regular income rate (higher)
- Long-term (held >1 year): taxed at preferential capital gains rate (lower)

**Best practice:** Keep detailed records of every transaction — date, amount, price at time of transaction. Use a crypto tax tool (Koinly, CoinTracker) and consult a tax professional.
